News.title: Millions of bees escape hives after truck moving them topples over – as locals told to stay indoors and avoid swarm
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

SWEET CHAOS Millions of bees escape hives after truck moving them topples over – as locals told to stay indoors and avoid swarm

MILLIONS of bees have escaped after a truck transporting hives overturned on the motorway.

In response, authorities issued a stark warning to Texas residents to stay indoors and avoid swarms at all costs.





The bizarre incident happened near the town of Mauriceville on Sunday.

Orange county emergency services said: “Everyone that lives in the [affected] area please remain indoors.

“An 18 wheeler carrying beehives has turned over and there is a heavy presence of bees in the area.”

Officials subsequently put out a call to all local beekeepers to help round up some two million insects.

Read more in World News GUN HORROR Nine dead and 38 hurt in shootings after bloody weekend across Chicago



Shocking photos showed beekeepers dressed in white protective clothing fighting to bring huge swarms under control.

“Not something ever want to see, but so nice to see beekeepers helping beekeepers,” Queen Bee Supply wrote on social media.



“From commercial outfits to backyard beekeepers, grateful for everyone that came out and helped.”

Authorities later shared an update on Sunday saying the bees were now being transferred to local beekeepers.

“Crews are continuing to safely transfer the hives on to transport trucks, which will be hauled to a local honey farm,” it said.

It added: “Residents in the immediate area are still encouraged to use caution.”

By some miracle, nobody was injured apart from the odd sting.



This is not the first unusual incident to happen on busy highways across the US.

In June, a truck in Tennessee hauling fireworks caught fire, triggering a surprise display.

In August, firefighters responded to a crash in which a truck carrying a load of ribeye steaks suddenly burst into flames.

News.title: Wes Streeting tipped as favourite to become Chancellor in Burnham government after ditching plan for leadership contest
News.content:
WES Streeting has been tipped as a top contender for Andy Burnham’s Chancellor after abandoning his own No10 plans.

The ex-Health Secretary is now the favourite, with Ed’s Miliband’s Treasury hopes said to have cooled over fears he could spook the markets.





Mr Streeting, who was seen as Mr Burnham’s main rival for PM just weeks ago, threw his support behind the new Makerfield MP just after Sir Keir Starmer resigned.

He revealed he had spoken at length with Mr Burnham and urged Labour to avoid a bruising summer leadership war.

Allies insist that no deal has been struck between them — but Mr Streeting told The Sun earlier this month that he would be delighted to serve in a Burnham Cabinet.

Mr Streeting’s views on strict fiscal rules, and thinking that politicians should be honest about spending limits, have won him admirers in the City.

Danni Hewson, of investment platform AJ Bell, said: “Wes Streeting’s centrist credentials could make him a popular choice to win over markets.”

Traders are already rattled by Sir Keir’s resignation.

Some investors have shunned long-term UK debt over fears that borrowing could now be ramped up — though gilt yields eased after Mr Streeting gave his backing to Mr Burnham.

Danni Hewson, head of financial analysis at AJ Bell, said Mr Streeting’s views had “endeared him to bond markets”.



She said: “Wes Streeting’s centrist credentials could make him a popular choice to win over markets, which have so far been muted in their response to the political upheaval.

“Whilst he hasn’t held any positions to flex his fiscal muscles, his work as Health Secretary gained plaudits from the public and he’s been vocal in his belief that politicians should be more honest about what the government can afford.”

Martin Beck, chief economic economist at WPI Strategy, added: “If Andy Burnham gets the keys to No10, his first test will be choosing a Chancellor who understands there is no magic money tree left.



“Taxes are already painfully high, public borrowing is high and the markets will not give a new Labour government endless room to spend.

“The next Chancellor, whether it is Wes Streeting or anyone else, cannot be another politician promising to solve every problem with another raid on taxpayers.”

News.title: Body of man in his 20s is found at popular park as cops set up cordon
News.content:
TRAGIC FIND Body of man in his 20s is found at popular park as cops set up cordon

A MAN in his twenties has been found dead in a busy Lancashire park.

Emergency services rushed to Williamson Park on Friday morning after reports that a man had been found “unresponsive”.



Lancashire Police said the man was pronounced dead at the scene.



The park was quickly cordoned off as officers and emergency crews launched an investigation, reports Lancs Live.

There are not believed to be any suspicious circumstances surrounding the death.

A police spokesperson said in a statement: “We were called at 7.55am on Friday 19th June to Williamson Park, Wyresdale Road, Lancaster, to a report that a man had been found unresponsive.

“The emergency services attended and very sadly, the man in his 20s was pronounced deceased at the scene.”



They continued: “Our thoughts are very much with this family and loved ones at this distressing time.

“The death is not being treated as suspicious, and a file will be prepared in due course for HM Coroner.”

News.title: No10 merry-go-round is like a reality show without the fun – we can’t keep upgrading PM like an iPhone
News.content:
AND so another excruciating, long run of the wearisome reality show that might as well be known as He’s The Prime Minister . . . Get Him Out Of Here! finally nears its end.

The numerous trials Sir Keir Starmer faced during his two-year shift as PM were not of the Bushtucker variety, but if they had been, you suspect his haul of stars would have left his campmates pretty starving.





I’m sure, at times, Keir would rather have joyfully chowed down on a kangaroo’s anus than dealt with the winter fuel allowance fiasco, or stuck his hand blindly into a nest of vipers rather than suffer the indignity of the release of the Mandelson files.

Still, the vipers got him in the end. Now, Andy Burnham looks set to be crowned King of the Jungle and here we go again for the next tedious series.

Some argued that when former Health Secretary Matt Hancock and Reform Leader Nigel Farage appeared on the real I’m A Celeb, it demeaned political office.

But in recent years, the whole vibe of the Westminster village has increasingly felt like a reality show — without the entertaining bits.

We have all the in-fighting from a revolving roster of underwhelming, moderately famous public figures voting each other in and out — without the light relief of Ant and Dec’s live links.

It’s like watching a non-stop procession of The Traitor’s Round Table banishments without the joy of obsessing over where Claudia Winkleman gets her cable-knit jumpers.

During the latest toppling of the latest PM, I found my mind constantly returning to a memory from childhood.

The year was 1990 and I was ten years old. I distinctly remember the moment our middle school humanities lesson was interrupted by the deputy headmistress going class to class to announce the news that Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher had resigned.





If my kids’ teachers interrupted classes every time a Westminster heavyweight fell on their sword, they would never reach the end of the syllabus.

But back then, Mrs Thatcher being forced out as Prime Minister did feel like a huge deal.

I had known no other reality. In fact at that point I probably thought blokes weren’t even allowed to lead the country so ensconced had she seemed in the role.

After her there was John Major, then there was Tony Blair and by that time I was old enough to vote.

By contrast, our new Prime Minster will be the SEVENTH my son has seen and he is only 12. By the time the next leader is installed in Downing Street, my five-year-old would have seen five.

This worries me a great deal because the boring stuff I care about, like economic stability, growth and ensuring my kids have an education to help them meet the challenges of a world remaking itself at a breakneck pace, all seems continually put on the backburner.

Meanwhile, politicians and advisers of all persuasions funnel their energy behind whichever new guy or gal is flavour of the month and who might stand a better chance of winning an election.

But a Prime Minister isn’t a ruddy iPhone, they shouldn’t be obsolete in two years and in need of an upgrade.

These cyclical feeding frenzies seem the new norm among the politicians, their special advisers, and, dare I say, journos who exist in the Westminster bubble and seem to bore very easily.



Labour seem to believe that Burnham’s resounding victory in Makerfield would automatically translate across the country at a general election. I’m not so sure.

A poll for The Times at the weekend found the majority of voters at a national level felt they knew barely anything about him.

Stay tuned, then, viewers for another reality-style eviction . . .

PICKY TWITS SUMMER has finally arrived with a vengeance. However, it is not the hot temperatures making me irritable, but the fact this means it’s the season of “picky bits”. As soon as the sun comes out, normally right-thinking people abandon all sensible notions of eating and race to buy tiny portions of cold, revolting, oily food. Little rubbery squid rings or olives swimming in oil, tiny dense omelettes, ash-dry balls of falafel that wick the moisture from your mouth. All of these dreadful items are usually purchased in plastic tubs as part of 3-for-2 deals, with half of the food left strewn in parks. And now M&S has declared this Saturday National Picky Bits Day. Horrendous. These snacks masquerading as meals fail to fill you up, whilst simultaneously making you feel sick. I’ll stick to a sandwich and an ice lolly, thanks.

Tom makes me Zen over wedding

I LOVE a celeb wedding. I pored over every detail of Dua Lipa and Callum Turner’s recent nuptials with the kind of attention to detail it would have required to sew the 480,000 beads on to the bride’s exquisite Chanel wedding gown.

Similarly, I gasped at Perrie Edwards’ stunning lace train as she wed footballer Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain. And, of course, I have followed all the madcap clues relating to Taylor Swift’s upcoming union to Travis Kelce.

So you can imagine my disappointment at the scant details shared of Tom Holland and Zendaya’s wedding.

After months of “have they/haven’t they” speculation during which fake AI photographs flew around the internet supposedly showing their big day, Tom finally confirmed they had.

He then refused to give more details.

I have a grudging respect for Tom and Zendaya’s spoilsport approach. Initially, they seemed an unlikely couple, she a statuesque Hollywood A-lister, he a slightly weedy, British bloke who grew up in an unremarkable suburb of London.



But the down-to-earth pair, who are often spotted popping to the supermarket near their home in London, seem to have brilliant chemistry and a refreshingly unstarry attitude.

DITCH PHONE AS TOY THIRTY years after I saw the first Toy Story movie as a 15-year-old, I found myself in a bizarre time warp taking my own three children to see the latest instalment this weekend. Surely I can’t be that old . . . The first movie told of retro cowboy doll Woody being replaced by whizzy new Space Ranger toy Buzz Lightyear. The latest film updates the theme, with kids preferring to stare at their devices. The theme is so in-step with the Government’s proposed ban on social media for under-16s that you wonder if they weren’t in on the marketing campaign. But the message left me thinking about my own behaviour around tech, not my children’s. In my family, I am by far the worst doomscroller, WhatsApper and meme-sharer, often glued to my phone trying to run multiple conversations at once or filling any spare moment getting sucked into watching all manner of pointless reels. Academic research suggests parental phone use may affect children’s language development, behaviour, emotional security and screen habits. It points to a problem many families will recognise – children are being told to look up from their screens by adults who often cannot. If we as parents are to enforce this ban, we need to crack down on ourselves first.

CHRIS IS ACE KARD

THE announcement that Chris Appleton has signed as the fourth celebrity for this year’s Strictly Come Dancing will no doubt be mostly met by cries of: “Who?”

Not from me. As a long-term viewer of The Kardashians, I am well versed in his work as a “conceptual hairdresser”, as the Beeb called him in its press release.

I long ago went down a Google rabbit hole finding out who the handsome Brit on the show was, who seems Velcro-ed to Kim’s side 24/7 a day.

Appleton has two kids from his first relationship before coming out as gay in his twenties and has travelled the world as Kim’s personal crimper.

A niche booking, you could say, but producers aren’t daft – they are clearly hoping the whole Kardashian crew will bring a dose of megawatt, front-row glam on a Saturday night.

MEN taking hair loss medication have complained it gives them moobs.

Fellas who took Finasteride reported the drug triggered the growth of breast tissue.

Boobs or baldness, it’s a tricky one, right lads?

Good to know it isn’t just women who feel they can’t win when it comes to ageing.

News.title: Andy Burnham is a fraud set to seize power like a tin-pot Oliver Cromwell – this ego trip is an insult to democracy
News.content:
WHO the hell does Andy Burnham think he is?

The so-called King of the North seems to believe he has a god-given right to waltz into Parliament, depose a recently elected PM and take over the country.





To be fair, nobody will shed a tear for Keir Starmer. Goodbye and good riddance.

But Burnham? The man’s a fraud, an empty suit. He stands for nothing – or not for more than five minutes.

His only experience outside the grubby world of politics is a short stint on a trade paper. Nobody, apart perhaps from Mrs Burnham, has ever viewed him as a coming Messiah.

And yet here he is, a tin-pot Oliver Cromwell, seizing absolute power without the consent of the British people.

Andy was not even in Parliament when Labour won in 2024. He had no role in writing its tissue-thin manifesto.

Now after breaking and entering, he wants a few weeks to dream up new ideas while Starmer carries on as phantom PM. What an image for a goggling world!

Never-Here Two-Tier Keir has dropped Britain in the mire, defenceless, bankrupt and at war with itself – a “nation of strangers”, as he rightly calls it.

But Burnham is no better. He is economically illiterate, hopelessly indecisive and alarmingly thin-skinned – just like Starmer.



Like the rest of the Labour Party since Alastair Campbell entered Downing Street, he is obsessed with football. He would rather talk about his beloved Everton than cutting the national debt or finding work for jobless school-leavers.

Aides in his last two bids for the Labour crown still shudder over chaos and incompetence of a man who couldn’t even beat Jeremy Corbyn.

In the five-week Makerfield by-election campaign, Andy talked incessantly about change. Not once did he explain what would change – or how.



This ego-trip is an insult to democracy.

Why should a man virtually unknown to the British voters become their leader without offering them a say in a general election?

Labour has paid a bitter price for picking one dud PM.

They deserve annihilation if they do it again.

News.title: I was part of Bawdsey Bay Five & uncovered £63k ‘pirate stash’…now we’re penniless after calling cops
News.content:
RICKY Hall will never forget the day it began raining money.

He was part of a five-man Environment Agency field team clearing sea defences on the Suffolk coastline, when they were showered with cash.



It happened four years ago when one of his colleagues was operating a remote-controlled lawn mower, which hit a brown leather case hidden in undergrowth.

Ricky, 66, said: “There was a loud bang and a colleague shouted out ‘We’re in the money’. I looked and there were bank notes flying in the air, it was raining money.

“We all started singing, ‘We’re in the money’. I’ll never forget it as long as I live.”



In total, £63,500 was found. A clue to its origins was laid out on the ground nearby in the shape of an arrow made with stones pointing towards where the bag lay.

The Treasure Island-style sign is suspected to have been left by criminals paying modern-day pirates smuggling drugs across the North Sea in high-powered inflatable boats.

Somehow, the bag was missed by the smugglers, leading to the windfall for Ricky and his four colleagues on Driftwood Beach, Bawdsey.

However, in a twist to make Long John Silver hopping mad, the Bawdsey Bay Five (BB5), as they are known, have been left without a penny.

After handing in the money to police, the BB5 were told they could not have it back even though it was never subject to a Proceeds of Crime Act order.



Ricky is now going to court to try to obtain a magistrate’s order under the rarely used Police and Property Act 1897, arguing that the money should be returned to them.

He says: “I am taking this court action on the principle of ‘finders keepers’ and to make sure the money is shared among the lads.

“We have been honest and have been treated badly for it. It does not belong to the police.”

Until the cash was discovered on August 17, 2022, Bawdsey’s main claim to fame was as the site of the world’s first operational radar station, established in 1937, and which played a vital role in the Battle of Britain.



Ricky’s team was cutting grass and clearing sea defence embankments around the erosion-plagued scenic coastal area, ten miles from Woodbridge, when they found the cash.

He recalls: “We were cutting the grass with a remote-controlled lawn mower which had a three-and-a-half foot rotor blade.

“I was standing on top of the sea defence embankment, and a colleague was at the bottom operating the machine when the money started flying.

“My colleague switched off the machine and we went to investigate.



“We found a brown leather case which had been shredded by the mower and inside it were bundles of cash.

“The money was mainly in £50 and £20 notes and was quite damp, so it must have been there a while.

“There was a guy on top of the sea defence embankment with his wife and their child and he started picking up money.

“We told him he could not take the money and he put it back down.

“Then we had a chat among the five of us about what to do with the cash. Two wanted to keep it, one wasn’t sure and two wanted to call the police. In the end we agreed to call the police.”



Ricky, now retired, said: “A uniformed female officer and an old detective turned up.

“It was the detective who noticed the arrow made from stones.

“The policewoman sealed the money in a bag and one of the guys signed for it. Then the police took it to a station property store. We were told that if nobody claimed it then we would receive it back in six months’ time.”

Under normal protocols, police return cash or valuables handed in if they remain unclaimed after three months.



An exception is if the money or booty is suspected to be the proceeds of crime.

To keep it, police must get a Proceeds of Crime Act order from a magistrate within 48 hours of seizing it, say the BB5.

Ricky is being assisted in his case by retired Essex police superintendent Steve Robinson.

He is a relative of one of the other four members of the BB5, who still work for the Environment Agency and wish to remain anonymous.

Steve says: “Suffolk Police should have got an order to seize that cash within 48 hours of taking control of it, but they never did.



“It was obviously criminal cash which had been left there for drugs. A kilo of cocaine at that time cost around 70,000 to 75,000 euros which would have fitted with the £63,500 found.

“It is likely that the bag was one of a number left there for cocaine brought from Holland.

“We’ll never know what happened, but the smugglers probably picked up some bags and couldn’t find one in the dark.

“Who knows, someone might even have ended up being killed over the loss of that money.

“The point is that even though the money very likely belonged to criminals, the police never declared it as such. Because they didn’t do that, they should have returned it to the Bawdsey Bay Five.”



After struggling to get any response from police, Steve says one of the BB5 was told by the female PC in March the following year that the money was linked to a Bank of England investigation.

Steve added: “The basis of this was that one of the bundles of cash was still in cellophane wrapping with a Bank of England stamp.

“It had clearly just been given out that way by a bank in the first place. There never was a Bank of England inquiry and the cash has never been linked to any criminal investigation.”



The cash — minus £1,250 of it destroyed by the mower — has been in a Suffolk Police account for at least three years. Steve says: “With interest, it would be worth around £75,000 now. It’s a lot of money for the five guys.”

He has made complaints to Suffolk Police and the Independent Office for Police Conduct about the handling of the case.

Steve says: “We have never received an adequate explanation over why the money can’t be returned.” Local MPs have also been lobbied but to no avail.

Ricky says: “We have been told the Suffolk Police and Crime Commissioner Tim Passmore will give the money to charities of his choice at some point.

“He could decide to even give us some reward from the money.



“But in my view it is not for him to decide what to do with the cash as it doesn’t belong to him. It belongs to us as the finders.”

Ricky has a hearing scheduled at Ipswich Magistrates’ Court in November to try to get an order for the return of the cash.

He believes there is a legal precedent to prove his case.

In 2019, staff at Sackers scrap metal yard near Ipswich discovered almost £20,000 in an old safe.

The money was handed over to Suffolk Police who did not give it back when it went unclaimed.



As the cash was never proved to be criminal, a magistrate ordered the money to be given back to the scrap dealer, who gave it to charity.

Steve said: “The magistrate must decide what is right and proper in the circumstances. This money has got to go somewhere and we believe the law is on the side of the Bawdsey Bay Five.”

In January this year, Steve and Ricky raised their case at a meeting of the Suffolk Police accountability and performance panel.

Suffolk Chief Constable Rachel Kearton told them she was limited in commenting by the impending court case, adding that a review into the “unusual set of circumstances” could follow the legal case.

Ricky says: “It is costing me money to go to court. I’m being threatened with having to pay Suffolk Police for their legal costs if I lose. But there is an important principle here.



“We are going to have mowers outside court with bags of Monopoly money to throw in the air.

“An injustice has been done and we are determined to highlight it.”

News.title: Burnham has no plan for Government & will end up just like Starmer… nothing will change until Labour learn vital lesson
News.content:
THERE will be plenty of commentators writing Keir Starmer’s political obituary over the coming days.

Appointing Peter Mandelson, failing to fund our armed forces properly, failing to cut welfare . . . I could go on.





But the fundamental issue is much simpler than many people realise.

Starmer confused winning a general election with having an agenda for government.

Winning an election is only ten per cent of what a Prime Minister needs to do to be successful.

You cannot exercise power if you do not first win it.

But the reason that so many Prime Ministers are failing is that our political system has become obsessed with campaigning for elections and forgotten how to govern.

We have become experts at polling, data and getting elected.

We have general elections, mayoral elections, Senedd elections, Holyrood elections, county elections and parish elections.

We have become exceptionally good at running campaigns.



But too many politicians no longer know how to make things work once they win.

This is what I am trying to do with my mission to Get Britain Working.

It is all about bringing common sense back into government.

Too often, we stop people using their judgment.

We force them to follow processes, tick boxes and procedures, until they end up doing obviously foolish things.



People stop thinking for themselves.

That is what happened to Keir Starmer.

It’s how we ended up with a government that found £4billion for walking and cycling, but can’t find the money for our armed forces.



A government that is potentially shortening the sentences of grooming gang perpetrators and culling ponies on Dartmoor.

And unless politicians learn the lesson that you need a plan for government, we will keep on getting the same failed governments.

It will probably happen to Andy Burnham.

He has no plan for government either.

Winning the Makerfield by-election does not make someone ready for No10 Downing Street.



The same applies to Nigel Farage. Reform talks endlessly about power, but power requires preparation.

Nigel Farage does not have enough serious candidates.

Many of the people he has recruited would struggle to pass the standards of someone appointed to run the village fete, let alone govern a country.

Reform has attracted some of the Conservatives who generated headlines and controversy, but not necessarily the people who know how to make government work.

They have no defence spokesman. No foreign affairs spokesman. Yet Farage is already calling for a general election.



That tells you everything you need to know about Reform.

Running the country is not the same as having arguments online.

The reason Keir Starmer has had to resign is ultimately about one thing: his own Defence Secretary publicly concluded that this government could not keep the country safe.



Anyone pretending this is about something else is not being serious.

We have Russia becoming increasingly aggressive towards Nato and firing on yachts in the English Channel.

HMS Dragon was stuck in a dry dock in Portsmouth when our airbases in Cyprus were under attack from Iranian missiles, after Labour paused the Conservative government’s defence plans and failed to produce a credible replacement plan.

Critical investment decisions are being delayed.

Confidence is draining away from the economy.



Labour are abandoning our oil and gas industry with a disastrous effect on British businesses.

At the same time, the Conservatives’ by-election victory in Aberdeen South showed that the British people often have more common sense than the politicians who claim to speak for them.

They understand that we do not have time for Labour to spend months engaged in internal party navel-gazing.

The country needs leadership now.

Keir Starmer clearly failed at the job. I wish him no ill will and I genuinely feel sorry for him.



But the timetable he has set out looks more like a farewell tour than a plan to grip the problems facing Britain.

Andy Burnham now needs to answer some serious questions.

Being Mayor of Manchester is a completely different job from being Prime Minister.



As mayor, he was given a budget and a defined set of responsibilities.

Running a country is different — you have to find the money, someone will always lose out, tough decisions have to be taken.

The question Labour MPs should be asking is not whether Andy Burnham can win elections, but whether he can govern.

Unless they, and the rest of the country, learn that lesson, Britain will keep on producing election winners and government failures.

The Conservative Party under my leadership has learned from what went wrong.



That is why I set out an Alternative King’s Speech last month. Not slogans. Not gimmicks. A serious programme of practical, common-sense legislation.

A Bill to leave the ECHR and finally get control of our borders. A Bill to drill our own oil and gas and bring down energy bills. A Bill to reform welfare and get people back to work.

And more than ten other Bills ready to go if the Conservatives were in government.

I know what needs to change. More importantly, I know how to do it and I have taken the time to do the work so that it actually happens.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Today, the Conservative Party is the only party offering the common sense reforms needed to get Britain working again and keep our country united.



Everyone else is offering division. Britain deserves better than that.

News.title: UK heatwave live: School closures confirmed as Met Office issues red extreme heat warning
News.content:
The Met Office has issued a rare red weather warning as temperatures could surge as high as 40C - which may mean we see the hottest day ever this week

A number of schools across the UK have confirmed school closures for tomorrow (Tuesday June 23) as temperatures soar. The Met Office has issued red warning for 'extreme heat' as it looks likely high temperature records could be broken this week.

The UK is set for its hottest June days on record as temperatures reach as high as 40C this week. Headteachers have raised concerns about the health and comfort of children in the extreme temperatures with a number of schools opting to close or shut early.

Official Department for Education guidance advises against closing schools and states that "schools could consider relaxing uniform rules during hot weather to make sure pupils are comfortable."

The Met Office has issued a red weather warning ahead of a spell of "exceptional" hot and humid weather this week. The red alert comes into force on Wednesday warns of temperatures rising as high as 40C in some places and is scheduled to last until 9pm on Thursday. The current temperature record is 40.3C in the UK, which was recorded in July 2022.

News.title: Jeremy Doku returns to UK on emergency flight for birth of first child
News.content:
Jeremy Doku returns to UK on emergency flight for birth of first child

Jeremy Doku has been criticised for saying he wants to leave Belgium's World Cup camp to be with his wife when she gives birth to their first child

View 2 Images Rudi Garcia, Jeremy Doku and Nathan Ngoy during Belgium's World Cup game against Egypt (Image: (DIRK WAEM / BELGA MAG / Belga / AFP via Getty Images))

Jeremy Doku is set to return to the Belgium squad after catching an emergency flight to London for the birth of his child. Doku jetted back to London at short notice to be alongside his wife Shireen as they welcomed their new baby boy, Praise, together.

‌



The Manchester City star missed his side’s 0-0 Group G draw against Iran on Sunday because of a respiratory illness but was cleared to fly back to London so he could be with his wife. Belgium team doctor Brahim Hacene said in a statement: "As he had already been receiving the appropriate medical treatment for several days, he was able to fly without any medical risk in order to be with his family during this very special moment.

‌



"He was accompanied by my colleague, Dr. Brecht De Coninck. Everything went perfectly, and the mother, father, and baby are all doing wonderfully. Jérémy will rejoin the group tomorrow evening in Seattle." While a statement from the Belgium FA confirmed: “Jeremy received news before [Sunday’s] match that the birth was imminent.

‌



“As he had already been receiving appropriate medical treatment for several days, he was able to fly without medical risk to be with his family during this very special moment.

“He was accompanied by my colleague, Dr Brecht De Coninck. Everything went perfectly, and the mother, father, and baby are all doing wonderfully. Jeremy will rejoin the squad [Tuesday] evening in Seattle.”

Lionel Messi admits World Cup heroics have left him worn out after breathtaking display READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



A post on Belgium’s X account also said: “Congratulations to Jeremy Doku and his family on the birth of their first son, Praise.

“With the approval of and accompanied by one of our team doctors, Jeremy travelled to London to be with his wife for this unique occasion. Jeremy will rejoin the squad tomorrow evening in Seattle as preparations continue for next match against New Zealand.”

Rudi Garcia’s side face New Zealand on Friday in their final World Cup match and need a win, after opening the tournament with two draws, to avoid being eliminated from the World Cup before the knockout rounds.

‌



On Sunday, French newspaper L'Equipe disavowed what many have described as 'disgraceful' comments by a female commentator who criticised Doku for wanting to leave the World Cup to be at the birth of his first child. The publication apologised to the winger in a statement late on Sunday and said the comments by France Pierron did not represent its values.

Pierron, speaking on the L'Equipe de Choc on Friday, said: “You can’t miss a World Cup. And now, you’re not going to the match to cut an umbilical cord?

“You have the chance to participate in a World Cup, and there are hundreds of footballers who would kill to be in your place.

‌



View 2 Images Journalist France Pierron (Image: (Stephane Cardinale - Corbis/Corbis via Getty Images))

“But you’re going to leave all that to go and witness the birth of your child, which is a disgusting moment. Excuse me, where the father is useless, he has a role as an extra.”

Later clarifying her comments, Pierron said: "In light of the very numerous reactions following my comments in 'L'Équipe de Choc' regarding Belgian footballer Jérémy Doku, I wish to provide a few clarifications. In it, I expressed a personal opinion, within the framework of a debate.

‌



"In it, I was expressing a personal opinion, within the context of a contentious exchange. These remarks commit only me and in no way reflect a collective position. I understand that they may have shocked, hurt, or wounded some of you, and I am sorry for that.

"My intention has never been to minimize the place or role of fathers with their partner and their child."

‌



Belgium boss Garcia had no issue with Doku flying back. Speaking ahead of the draw against Iran: “He can’t play, and so we’ll be playing without him. I knew since Friday that he won’t be playing.

“I don’t want to get players to play if they’re not medically up for the game. I can get players to play even if they’re not 100 percent physically, but 100 percent medically is more important.”

News.title: Keir Starmer resigns: Andy Burnham confirms leadership bid after tearful Prime Minister sets out timeline to leave number 10
News.content:
Andy Burnham has confirmed he will stand in a bid to succeed Keir Starmer as Labour leader after the Prime Minister announced his resignation today, having acknowledged his support in the party had drained away

Andy Burnham will stand to replace Keir Starmer as Labour leader after the Prime Minister announced his No10 exit this morning.

Burnham, who has now been sworn in as an MP, followed up Starmer's resignation speech by describing it as the beginning of a transition”, adding he will “put myself forward as part of this process”.

Immediately after Burham's announcement, former health secretary Wes Streeting said he would back him for the party leadership, saying “he can win the fight of our lives against the forces of nationalism”. He had been seen as a potential rival to Burnham for the top job.

Their moves came after the PM took to the podium in Downing Street to announce his decision to quit and laid out plans for leaving office in a bid to ensure an "orderly transition" in running the country, with nominations opening on July 9 in a contest to replace him.

Voice cracking with emotion, Starmer said becoming Prime Minister had been the “proudest moment of my life” but accepted: "The question my party is asking now is whether I am best placed to lead us into the next general election - I have heard the answer from my parliamentary party and I accept that answer with good grace. Every decision I have taken has been about putting the country I love first. That is why I will resign as leader of the Labour Party."

The Prime Minister had been bunkered down at Chequers with his wife Victoria over the weekend weighing up his future and she was at his side as he announced his resignation. They both stood before No 10 before going back in, again to loud applause and cheers for his team gathered outside.

Burnham returned to Westminster this afternoon to be sworn in as an MP in the wake of his emphatic victory in the Makerfield by-election.

News.title: UK weather maps show Arctic 4C cold blast looms after scorching heatwave
News.content:
UK weather maps show Arctic 4C cold blast looms after scorching heatwave

Weather maps are showing a dramatic cold blast is set to hit the UK next month, with temperatures plummeting hugely in some areas across 22 counties, including Cambridgeshire

View 3 Images Temperatures are expected to fall significantly, including in Brighton in East Sussex (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Mirror)

An Arctic cold snap looms after this week's blistering heatwave, weather maps show.

‌



Although the mercury is expected to hit 40C this week, during which rare red weather warnings are in place, the picture is expected to change signficantly. Fresh maps from WXCHARTS indicate that temperatures are set to nosedive on July 4 - just under a fortnight away.

‌



According to these latest weather maps, most of the country may get above the high teens at around 6am, with lows of just 4C in the Scottish Highlands and single-digit temperatures across almost the entire rest of the country. The Northwest of England and the Northeast of England are expected to be the chilliest regions south of the border, with the mercury dropping to around 9C.

‌



And, further south, temperature lows may only just nudge into the low-to-mid teens, with 14C in East Anglia and lows of 13C in the Southwest of England and northern Wales. Londoners and those along the south coast could also face a rather nippy 12C at 6am on July 4. These figures are hugely different to this week's scorching blast, as 31.8C has already been recorded - at Heathrow Airport in west London - and it is expected to get warmer.

View 3 Images Cooler air will hover over the UK on the morning of July 4, maps suggest (Image: WXCHARTS)

‌



The Met Office forecast for June 17 to July 6 cautions of "changeable conditions" at the start of next month as "Atlantic lows move in from the west", but with "transient periods of high pressure" that will lead to spells of rain.

The forecast reads: "Fairly changeable conditions at first with periods of rain and showers, and there could be some thundery outbreaks at times. There will likely be some drier and brighter spells though.", reports the Express.

"Into July changeable conditions are likely to continue as Atlantic lows move in from the west, but with transient periods of high pressure. This will lead to spells of rain and cloud interspersed with more settled periods.

Article continues below

"Temperatures remain widely above average, and the far southeast may retain some of the hot temperatures at first, but likely cooler than the preceding few days."

News.title: Met Office reveals when heatwave will end as temperatures to drop by 15C in days
News.content:
Met Office reveals when heatwave will end as temperatures to drop by 15C in days

England and Wales will be engulfed by scorching temperatures as a rare red warning for extreme heat has been issued by the forecaster, along with an amber one

View 3 Images People have been asked to keep out of the sun between 11am and 3pm (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

The Met Office has revealed when the heatwave will end as England and Wales are bracing for extreme temperatures.

‌



This comes as an amber weather warning for extreme heat came into force this morning and will remain in place until Thursday. Areas affected by the amber warning will see temperatures exceed 30C and potentially reach 38-40C.

‌



A red warning for extreme heat will also affect a number of regions on Wednesday and Thursday, with temperatures exceeding 37C and likely rising to 38-40C in some areas.

‌



Almost 100 areas will be affected by the severe weather conditions, as people have been urged to keep out of the sun between 11am and 3pm, when the sun is strongest.

But England and Wales will finally be able to breathe properly again from Saturday onwards, when more bearable temperatures are expected.

‌



According to the Met Office, temperatures will be lower by even 15C on Saturday, compared to the peak of the heatwave on Wednesday, when temperatures of up to 40C are expected.

View 3 Images Large parts of the country will see temperatures in the mid- to high- 30s as the heatwave takes hold on Wednesday and Thursday (Image: netweather.tv)

View 3 Images Weather maps show temperatures dropping significantly by Saturday June 28 after heatwave conditions this week (Image: netweather.tv)

Article continues below

Giving an outlook for Saturday through to July 6, the forecaster said: "Fairly changeable conditions at first with periods of rain and showers, and there could be some thundery outbreaks at times.

"There will likely be some drier and brighter spells though. Into July changeable conditions are likely to continue as Atlantic lows move in from the west, but with transient periods of high pressure.

"This will lead to spells of rain and cloud interspersed with more settled periods. Temperatures remain widely above average, and the far southeast may retain some of the hot temperatures at first, but likely cooler than the preceding few days."

News.title: Mum, 32, given terminal diagnosis after GPs blamed symptoms on parenthood
News.content:
Mum, 32, given terminal diagnosis after GPs blamed symptoms on parenthood

EXCLUSIVE: Mum Chloe Houghton, 32, discovered she has terminal stage 4 lung cancer months after first visiting her GP, who dismissed her lump as a harmless cyst and blamed the symptoms on toddler exhaustion

View 6 Images Chloe has never touched a cigarette but was diagnosed with a cancer predominantly found in smokers (Image: Chloe Houghton)

After being told she has incurable cancer, a heartbroken mum-of-two has told how she can barely look at her young children, aged one and four, without feeling an overwhelming sense of guilt that she is about to leave them behind.

‌



Chloe Houghton, a fit and active 32-year-old beauty salon owner, received the devastating diagnosis after discovering a lump on her chest - which she was repeatedly reassured was just a harmless cyst.

‌



However when she finally had it removed, doctors diagnosed her with stage four Small Cell lung cancer, after discovering that the disease had already spread.

‌



"I've never smoked or vaped in my life but all you need for lung cancer is a pair of lungs," Chloe, from Northamptonshire, told the Daily Mirror.

Chloe first noticed the small mass while in the shower. Though it was only a few millimetres wide at the time, it began growing rapidly and became painful when she picked up her son.

Doctor says all Brits under 40 must make key change as deadly heart attacks surge READ MORE :

6 View 6 Images Chloe had no idea she had lung cancer after doctors repeatedly rebuffed her (Image: Chloe Houghton) 6 View 6 Images She noticed the lump but was initially told it was just a cyst (Image: Chloe Houghton)

‌



A doctor initially told Chloe the lump was likely just a bit of cartilage. Because the mass moved when she pressed it, she was assured it was a "good" sign and highly unlikely to be cancerous.

Following a series of follow-up visits to the doctor and blood tests that all came back clear, Chloe pushed to have the lump removed in August 2025.

"It was getting bigger and you could notice it on my chest so I was having to wear higher neckline tops to cover it," she explained. "I wanted it off because it was hurting me when I picked my son up."

‌



After waiting weeks without receiving a surgery date, Chloe sought a second opinion from a different doctor. This GP referred her to a sarcoma clinic as a protocol, and booked her in for general surgery.

By February 2026, Chloe was still waiting for the operation, and the lump had expanded to two centimetres. During a hospital consultation, her mother told the doctor that Chloe's weight had dropped down from 10 stone to just seven.

Alarmed by the rapid weight loss, the consultant ordered an urgent CT scan of her chest, abdomen and pelvis. Six weeks later, the results flagged an abnormality on her lungs that needed further investigation.

‌



On the day that the chest lump was finally removed, the consultant admitted he was far more worried about her lungs than the mass itself, which he suspected was an infected cyst.

Three weeks later, Chloe received an unexpected call telling her to meet with the consultant "as soon as possible" and to bring a relative with her.

Accompanied by her mother and her husband, former firefighter Jamie who she married last July, Chloe received the shattering results.

‌



The biopsy showed she had neuroendocrine sarcoma.

"The consultant said it was a secondary cancer," Chloe said. "The primary cancer was in my lung. What they had removed was the tumour that had already spread outside of the lung into my chest."

Initially doctors were hopeful, suggesting chemotherapy followed by surgery to remove the cancerous part of the lung, because she was young, fit and healthy. Chloe was told that if she had been an older smoker, doctors would have considered lung cancer as a possibility much sooner.

‌



However, the optimism was brutally short-lived. A week later, her lung cancer nurse called with devastating news: the mass was Small Cell lung cancer - an aggressive, fast-growing form of the disease that accounts for 10% to 15% of cases and is almost exclusively linked to tobacco use in older adults. Because it had already metastasised, surgery was completely off the table.

6 View 6 Images Chloe had the lump on her wedding day - with no idea it would turn out to be cancer (Image: Chloe Houghton) 6 View 6 Images Now she's on a mission to share the message to women to listen to their bodies and always advocate if they believe something is wrong (Image: Chloe Houghton)

‌



A subsequent meeting with her oncologist confirmed that the advanced cancer would "significantly" reduce her life expectancy. As the cancer had spread outside of her lung, it meant they weren't able to operate and that it was "a case of chemotherapy and immunotherapy for as long as your body can tolerate it."

Chloe said: "I got upset straight away and all I said was 'I've got a one-year-old and a four-year-old. I'm not going to see them grow up, am I?'

"He turned around to me and said 'It would be incredibly cruel for me to say that you will'. Then everything just sort of stopped around me.

‌



"After that, I didn't hear anything, because in my head all I kept thinking was 'I'm going to die. I'm not going to see my kids grow up.' It was just horrid."

With her life completely turning upside down, Chloe was also told she wouldn't be able to work - and handed a SR1 form - a medical report that provides evidence that a patient is nearing the end of life in order to fast-track assistance.

She said: "That's when I knew how serious it really was. The nurse told me not to think too much into it, but it will mean I am entitled to some support financially and mentally.

‌



Tragically, it was a form her family know all too well. Chloe had lost her dad to pulmonary fibrosis just a year prior, and he had been given the exact same paperwork, meaning her mother knew instantly that the condition was untreatable.

View 6 Images Chloe is now undergoing chemotherapy

Because Chloe has unknowingly been living with untreated cancer since August 2025, doctors can't give her an exact prognosis. Small Cell lung cancer typically carries a life expectancy of just a few months without intervention, meaning her survival depends entirely on how her body responds to treatment.

‌



She began chemotherapy on June 2nd this year - the day before her 32nd birthday.

"I have good days and bad days but on the whole I'm okay," said Chloe. "It has put things into perspective for me. I'm just trying to enjoy the time that I've got."

According to The Union for International Cancer Control (UICC), lung cancer is the leading cause of death due to cancer worldwide. Significantly, the number of cases is rising alarmingly for women - especially younger non-smokers. This trend is exacerbated by the fact that early stage symptoms are often subtle and mistaken for benign respiratory issues.

‌



In Chloe's case, her early symptoms were misdiagnosed, with her GP brushing off her extreme fatigue and breathlessness as the exhaustion from raising toddlers. Her sudden inability to eat was misdiagnosed as a stomach ulcer, for which she was booked for an endoscopy.

Since starting chemotherapy, these symptoms have disappeared.

Despite her terminal diagnosis, Chloe is channelling her remaining energy into helping others through TikTok, sharing her story openly to advocate for women's health.

‌



" This is a really rubbish situation, but it could be worse. I can't change the card that I've been dealt," Chloe said. "I can only change how I respond to it right now. So that's why if I can help spread some awareness and help just one person.

"As women, you just have to keep pushing and advocating if you know something is wrong. I asked my consultant why it didn't show up in any blood tests he told me it's because this type of cancer doesn't show up in blood. We need to do more to help women who are worried about their health."

She added: "All I would say to people is to be very self-aware of your own body. Obviously, you should always be checking for lumps and for things that aren't your normal. And if you're not happy with something, you have to push for yourself."

‌



Key symptoms

Symptoms in the early stages are usually mild but rarely disappear. These include a new or worsening lingering cough for more than three weeks, shortness of breath during normal activities such as climbing stairs, frequent or recurring chest infections, voice hoarseness, unexplained fatigue or mild chest discomfort.

Small cell lung cancer is an aggressive, fast-growing type of lung cancer that accounts for about 10% to 15% of all lung cases. According to Macmillan, it's traditionally linked to tobacco use and has a high tendency to spread rapidly to other parts of the body.

But Chloe had never smoked or vaped in her life, and sadly young, healthy non-smoking women are becoming a higher statistic for lung cancer. Screening is now available for people over 55 with a history of smoking, but women like Chloe are only being diagnosed once the cancer has spread.

‌



According to Cancer Research UK, lung cancer is the second most common cancer in women with around 24,700 new cases every year - accounting for 13pc of all new female cancer cases in the UK.

While mortality rates have decreased by 40pc since the 1970s due to falling smoking rates among men, the incidence of lung cancer in females increased by more than 62pc.

Experts are still exploring exact causes, but hormones could also play a factor for women, as well as indoor air pollution, caused by wood-burning stoves and biomass fuels used for cooking and heating, has also been identified as a significant risk factor.

‌



Outdoor air pollution is believed to cause around one in 10 lung cancer cases in the UK. Doctors believe women's smaller lungs and narrower airways can lead to a higher concentration of pollutants becoming trapped. London is the most polluted city in Europe, and fifth worldwide from fumes and gases.

Experts suggest that genetic mutations also have a part to play. Research from the Francis Crick Institute suggest that air pollution might "wake up" dormant cells in the lungs that carry these cancer-causing mutations, promoting their growth.

Chloe has also set up a GoFundMe to help with medical costs, if she needs them, or to help go towards not being able to work, and providing for her family. You can find her fundraiser here.

Article continues below

For anyone worrying about lung cancer, it's always recommended to speak with your GP or a health professional. For more information, you can visit the Cancer Research website here.

News.title: 'I quit the UK for life abroad because I couldn't see a future amid cost-of-living crisis'
News.content:
'I quit the UK for life abroad because I couldn't see a future amid cost-of-living crisis'

Ebony Joseph left Southend-on-Sea, Essex, and moved to the Caribbean island of Saint Lucia in 2025 after becoming disillusioned with life in the United Kingdom

View 4 Images Ebony Joseph left Southend-on-Sea for St Lucia in 2025

A woman became so disillusioned with life in the United Kingdom she quit the country for a new life abroad.

Ebony Joseph, 30, swapped Southend-on-Sea, Essex, for the north of the Caribbean island of Saint Lucia on April 30, 2025, after struggling with her mental health and growing increasingly fed up with life in Britain.

The pastry chef felt trapped in a relentless cycle of working purely to keep up with bills, having long since abandoned any hope of ever getting on the property ladder. But, following a holiday to Saint Lucia a year before, during which she fell head over heels for the island's relaxed way of life, stunning scenery and exciting business prospects, Ebony took a bold leap of faith and started afresh abroad.

Now, more than a year later, she says her energy levels have soared, she's happier than she's ever been, and she's working towards launching her very own tour company and interactive travel guide.

View 4 Images Ebony is pictured in Saint Lucia

Ebony says a night out for dinner in the UK could easily set her back £100, yet in Saint Lucia she can eat out for as little as £5. The young woman, who was granted full St Lucian citizenship in September 2025 through her father's family roots, said: "I was earning decent money in the UK but no matter how much I earned, it felt like I was never getting any further forward.

"I couldn't see a future where I could afford my own property and I felt like I was just going to work to survive and pay bills. My mental health wasn't great and I was feeling really low. I realised nobody was going to change my life for me.

"I told my mum I needed to do something different. It was a scary decision, but I knew I had to take the chance. I am so glad I did it because it means I quit Essex for Saint Lucia. I eat out for £5 a night in a tropical paradise."

View 4 Images The pastry chef swapped Essex for a tropical paradise

Ebony first set foot onSaint Lucia as a tourist, where she struck up a friendship with a local contact named Sisi, who later helped her find her footing when she made the permanent move.

With just £2,000 in savings to her name, Ebony upped sticks and crossed the Atlantic, leaning on the generosity of friends and islanders while she got herself established.

She said: "If I hadn't had somewhere to stay when I arrived, I would've been in trouble. I survived on what I had and sold a few cakes here and there. People helped me out and I made some really good connections."

Though she studied cookery at school, Ebony had spent several years working in administration for a construction firm in England before opting to pursue her passion for food professionally.

In May 2026, she secured a position as a pastry chef at a hotel after wowing an executive chef with one of her cheesecakes and her impressive CV.

She said: "I ended up making a cheesecake for an executive chef. He tried it, looked at my CV and offered me a job. Facebook is a huge way of finding work out here and that's how a lot of opportunities come up."

View 4 Images Ebony says her mental health has improved

Despite the financial hurdles that came with relocating, Ebony insists the lifestyle she enjoys in Saint Lucia far outweighs any monetary sacrifices. She believes the island's outdoor lifestyle and deep connection with nature have made a tremendous difference to her overall wellbeing.

She said: "In England, if I was feeling low, I'd stay indoors. Now, if I'm having a bad day, I can go for a swim or spend time at the beach. As soon as the sun comes out, I want to be up and doing something. I've got so much more energy.

"There is so much free stuff to do here. You can have a cookout by the river, spend time at the beach and really appreciate what you have in life.

"You aren't spending on things to do as much because Saint Lucia is beautiful, and you and a friend could go out for a meal in the UK where it costs you £100 but in Saint Lucia you can go for a big meal and pay well under £20 for the two of you."

‌



Ebony also reveals she much prefers the culture in Saint Lucia, where she feels people place far greater importance on community, wellbeing and personal development.

She added: "There is more to life than working nine to five and partying every weekend. I wanted to surround myself with positive people and build something for myself. My friends and family say I look happier and healthier. I've lost weight and I feel better in myself too."

Reflecting on her journey, Ebony says relocating abroad was one of the boldest decisions she has ever made — yet one she will never regret.

Article continues below

She said: "Life is full of risks and sometimes you don't know what the outcome will be. I thought I had a 50-50 chance, but if it didn't work out, I'd just be back where I started.

"I didn't want to look back on my life and wonder 'what if?'

"My advice is simple - do what's best for you. The only person who can change your life is you. Take the risk, because if you don't, you'll never know what could have happened."

News.title: Olympic and Paralympic stars back Northern Games bid

In their statement, the athletes hail the north of England's "world-class venues", claiming it can build on the legacy of London 2012.

"The International Olympic Committee and International Paralympic Association's multi-city model makes a distributed Games more viable than ever before," they write.

"A 'Great North' Games would be a national Games. It would bring the country together in common purpose. It would showcase the very best of Great Britain.

"We believe that hosting a Games in the North of England in 2040 would be a moment of renewal and confidence for the entire United Kingdom. We are proud to add our voices to this vision and to support a Northern Games that would inspire generations to come."

Ex-gymnast Beth Tweddle, and former athletes Sir Brendan Foster, Steve Cram and Allison Curbishley are among other signatories.

In February, a group of northern political leaders urged the government to ensure any future Olympic bid would be based in the region, claiming there was a "compelling" case.

North East Mayor Kim McGuinness said: "The support of athletes who have represented Great Britain on the biggest stage of all is hugely significant. They understand better than anyone the power of the Olympic and Paralympic Games to inspire, unite and transform lives.

"A Great North Olympics would be a global showcase, powered by the pride and participation of Northern communities, leaving a legacy of prosperity, unity and renewal. This growing movement of support shows the strength of feeling behind the idea and the opportunity it presents for the whole country.

"We're grateful to every athlete who has added their name to this vision and look forward to working together as we take the next steps."

After rowing on the escalators of Boston’s South Station and at Boston Stadium, Norway fans have taken their epic tradition to the heart of New York City — and disrupted a summer solstice yoga class in the process.

Ahead of the team’s Monday night World Cup match against Senegal at New York New Jersey Stadium, Norway fans gathered Sunday to perform their iconic Viking Row on Times Square’s famous red steps.

Dozens of yogis were being led in a special practice honoring the start of summer, just feet from where hundreds of Norway fans were settled on the steps carrying out their cultural tradition of cheering, chanting, and of course, rowing. Some bystanders captured video of the Norwegians even joining in on some of the yoga poses.

Only hours later, video emerged of the Norwegians at it again — but this time on the floor of a moving subway car during Monday’s rush hour commute.

Videos of both rows have gone viral on social media as World Cup fever continues to sweep across the U.S.

open image in gallery Norway fans took their iconic Viking Row to New York City's Times Square ( Reuters )

“Incredible spirit. They are everywhere bringing joy to America and smiles to the world,” one person wrote on X of the subway row while another agreed, “NYC has really come alive with the World Cup energy, feels like the whole city is part stadium, part street festival. You’ve got fans everywhere, flags in the subways, packed bars and random match chants breaking out on corners like it’s normal life now.”

“2026 WC just changed the soccer culture of USA. Great influence. Thank you European soccer fans,” someone else wrote.

Others — true New Yorkers, perhaps — were quicker to take note of the fact that the Norwegians willingly sat on the dirty floor of a subway car.

“The filth these people are subjecting themselves to is unimaginable,” one person wrote on X.

open image in gallery Norway fans rowed just feet from where a summer solstice yoga class was happening ( Reuters )

“If only they knew the things that subway floor has endured over the years,” a second wrote while a third said, “There's team loyalty and then there's sit in biohazard subway floor team loyalty.”

Norway — appearing in the tournament for the first time in 28 years — won their first World Cup match in dominant fashion, defeating Iraq 4-1. Striker Erling Haaland's performance caused earth tremors in his home country after he netted two goals in the first half.

The goals sparked widespread joyous celebrations across Norway, where fans watched the match unfold at midnight.

Next, Norway is scheduled to take on Senegal in a pivotal group stage match Monday night. The team will then head back to Boston to square off against France in their final group stage match, slated for Friday.

Donald Trump on Monday furiously blamed “vandals” with sharp objects for the growing mess that has overtaken his project to renovate the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.

At an unrelated White House event, a reporter asked Trump about the ongoing state of the pool. The structure, which is the length of multiple city blocks, has been under renovation for weeks after Trump decided to drain the pool and had the surface spray-painted with an aqua blue coating used in swimming pools.

Photos and videos over the past week have shown chunks of that coating separating and floating up to the surface amid a swamp-green mess of algae that National Parks Service employees are desperately battling.

Trump claimed on Monday that a 300-foot long “slit” had appeared in the pool coating, which he attributed to a box cutter or knife and claimed that the National Parks Service was investigating. Reporters have not independently confirmed his account of the damage.

“No, we had vandalism...no, vandals,” he responded, when asked who was responsible for the problems. “We have a 290-, I think 300-foot slit right through, probably a box cutter or a knife of some kind.”

open image in gallery Donald Trump blamed vandals for the ongoing state of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool on Monday ( AFP/Getty )

According to Trump, the pool may need to be drained and repainted again.

The project has ballooned into a $14 million money hole for the administration, which has included the effort to resurface and repair the famously-leaky Reflecting Pool in the president’s broader campaign to beautify downtown Washington, D.C.

open image in gallery A worker cleans algae and chunks of paint from the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool on Monday ( AFP/Getty )

open image in gallery A man is arrested after shouting at police patrolling the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool on Monday. The scene has become a fixture for D.C. residents ( AFP/Getty )

Employees with the park surface have been unable to clear the pool of algae since the pool was refilled and the continued issues facing the project have become somewhat of a fixation for D.C. residents, reporters and others bemusedly watching the situation from afar.

Reporters have not been able to verify any acts of actual vandalism within the pool, which at times has been fenced off as workers continue repainting and de-algaefication efforts.

The president was challenged to provide proof of his claims of vandalism at his event on Monday, and claimed that the existence of the “slit” which he described in varying sizes was proof itself; reporters have not seen it for themselves.

“When you have a 350 foot slit, do you think that's proof?” Trump asked CBS’s Ed O’Keefe, who responded: “Reporters have been down there today looking for that slit you mentioned. There's no evidence [of it].”

“All you have to do is see the parks department. They'll show it to you,” the president shot back.

The Independent reached out to the Parks Service for comment.

A handful of arrests have been publicly reported at the Reflecting Pool since the project began, but none for the kind of large-scale vandalism Trump has claimed. One former Olympian, David Hearn, was arrested on the scene after he claimed to have touched some of the peeled-off pool coating surface out of curiosity. Hearn denied to the Daily Mail that he was guilty of vandalism, as the administration charged.

“It's a completely unfounded accusation,” he said. “We've already heard many lies from this administration…That's just another lie.”

Critics of the project say the blue paint is a waste, and transforms the original intended look of the memorial.

Trump, however, is going full steam ahead with his renovation efforts and recently also announced plans to extend the Lincoln Memorial down to the Potomac River waterfront with a “promenade” he claimed was part of the architects’ original intent.

Conservative commentator Tucker Carlson is officially breaking with the Republican Party after spending decades as one of its most influential backers in the media.

On a recent episode of the Can’t Be Censored podcast, Carlson accused the party of “treasonous” actions and putting the interests of corporate donors and Israel above those of American citizens, especially regarding the Iran war.

“I would not support the Republican Party,” Carlson said. “There’s no chance I would support the Republican Party. I’m not going to support the Democratic Party — I don’t know what I’m going to do.”

“I voted Republican my entire life,” the podcaster continued. “I worked at Fox News, CNN, MSNBC. I’ve been a consistent defender for 35 years of the Republican Party, — I mean, a very consistent defender. There’s no defending this because it’s amoral and it’s exactly the opposite of what a political party in a democracy is charged with doing, which is representing its own voters, its own citizens, its own nation. And they’re not doing that.”

Carlson added that his defection, as well as polling showing the Iran war is unpopular, should serve as a wake-up call for the Republican Party.

open image in gallery Tucker Carlson says he can no longer support the Republican or Democratic parties ( AFP/Getty )

“If I’m out, then I think a lot of other people are out,” he said.

The Independent has contacted the Republican National Committee and White House for comment.

Carlson’s comments come after months of public feuding between him and party leaders.

In April, he accused the Trump administration of failing to run the country well and pursuing unnecessary foreign wars, publicly apologizing for having campaigned on Trump’s behalf.

Carlson said he was “tormented by it” and that he was “sorry for misleading people.”

That month, Carlson also criticized the president after he told Iran to “open the F***in’ Strait” of Hormuz or they would be “living in Hell.”

“Who do you think you are?” Carlson said on his show. “You’re tweeting out the f-word on Easter morning?

open image in gallery Carlson has been feuding with the president for months over the Iran war and Israel ( AFP/Getty )

This spring, amid Carlson’s frequent scathing criticism of the Iran war and influence of Israel on U.S. foreign policy, President Trump fired back that Carlson had “lost his way” and was no longer a part of the MAGA movement.

“I knew that a long time ago, and he's not MAGA. MAGA is saving our country,” the president said in an interview in March.

Former congressman Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene has suffered a similar falling out with the party and the president, in part over positions on foreign wars and Israel.

"What the American people voted for with MAGA was to put the American people first,” she said in a November interview on CNN. “Stop sending foreign aid, and stop being involved in foreign wars...They very much deserve to be put first. Cost of living is far too high. Health insurance is completely out of control, and that’s – those are two issues I’ve been very vocal on for months and months now.”

She has also accused the Trump administration of backing Israel’s “genocide” in Gaza.

open image in gallery The Iran war has remained highly unpopular with voters, polling shows ( AFP/Getty )

Israel has been a consistent wedge between Carlson and much of the GOP, and the podcaster faced allegations of antisemitism for his friendly 2025 interview with white supremacist Holocaust denier Nick Fuentes.

A large majority of Americans want the Iran war to end and think the costs of the war did not justify the result, according to a CBS poll released on Sunday.

Love Island USA fans are calling on the show to remove one of the new Casa Amor bombshells from the cast after resurfaced video appears to show her saying a racial slur.

Alannah Keyser, a 21-year-old film student, was introduced during Sunday’s episode as one of the six new girls brought in for the hit dating show’s famous Casa Amor twist, which was meant to shake up the relationships that have been established in the three weeks of season eight so far.

But just hours after audiences saw Keyser dressed in an angel costume while she flirted with the boys in Fiji, a 10-second undated video began circulating on social media that appeared to show her mouthing the N-word as she sang along to lyrics at a Miami party.

The origins of the video remain unclear, but the backlash was swift. Allegations against Keyser escalated further with screenshots emerging that allegedly show Keyser using the N-word in conversations online.

As fans demand that Peacock remove Keyser from the show — like they did most recently with Vasana Montgomery, who was kicked out of the villa days before this season’s premiere when video emerged of her using a racial slur — criticism has mounted even more after fans of the show pointed out that during the episode, Keyser refused to kiss KC, Corbin and Sincere, the three Black contestants, but kissed the other three cast members.

Alannah Keyser is facing backlash after a resurfaced video appears to show her saying the N-word ( Peacock )

One fan wrote on X: “Nah I’m sorry that Alannah chick has GOT to go. She was straight up racist to the black guys during that challenge. That’s a fact. She has to go ! I was legit uncomfortable and it made me emotional. Like she’s one of those white people. Gross.”

“There have been folks who used slurs in their past,” another said. “But Alannah not only did that, she’s also refusing to engage with the men of color the same way she does with the white men. It’s blatant racism. And it’s not fair to subject the Islanders or the viewers to that.”

One person wrote on Reddit: “Are the casting directors just terrible at their job or is it a rite of passage to be a bigot???”

Keyser’s potential exit from the show would make her the fourth person in the last year to be removed from Love Island USA due to resurfaced evidence of them using a racial slur.

Although online rumors insist that Keyser has been removed from the show ahead of Monday night’s episode, Peacock has not confirmed any change to the casting yet, and fans will have to wait until further episodes air to learn whether or not she has been given the boot.

Drinking fruit juice, soda and other sweet beverages during childhood may raise the risk of high blood pressure in adulthood, according to new research published Monday.

A study by the American Heart Association of more than 25,000 Americans aged 9-16 over 25 years revealed that just two or more 12-ounce servings a day raised their risk for developing high blood pressure by 52 percent compared with those who consumed fewer than three servings each week.

High blood pressure – when the force of blood pushing against vein walls is too high – contributes to a heightened risk of heart and kidney disease, stroke and dementia. Over 125 million American adults live with high blood pressure, according to the association.

“Dietary habits in early life can have lasting health consequences,” Dr. Vasanti Malik, an adjunct faculty member at the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, said in a statement.

”High blood pressure is also emerging earlier in life, with growing rates being seen in younger adults, in children and adolescents, which highlights the importance of early detection and prevention.”

open image in gallery Drinking fruit juice and other sweet beverages as a kid may greatly raise the risk of high blood pressure later in life, researchers said. High blood pressure raises the risk of heart and kidney disease ( Getty Images/iStock )

Drinking 12 ounces of juice a day was tied to a 35 percent higher risk than those who drank less than one serving a week, and soda and sports drinks had a 23 percent and 36 percent higher risk, respectively.

One juice stood out above the rest; each daily serving of orange juice was associated with a 20 percent higher risk, while other juices were not.

But the researchers said that orange-flavored drinks with added sugars may have been misreported as orange juice.

Study participants tracked their food and drink intake and other health factors, taking questionnaires every 1-4 years. They also reported their blood pressure and researchers developed models showing the effects of different drinks.

Still, it’s not how much you’re drinking that matters the most, it’s what, American Heart Association volunteer expert Dr. Amit Khera explained.

“As has been seen in adults, the total amount of fructose seems less important for the development of hypertension than the type of food where it is consumed, so sugar-sweetened beverages and fruit juice relate to increased risk, while whole fruit does not,” said Khera.

“Secondly, there has been a misconception about fructose in general being harmful for cardiovascular health regardless of the source, and that fruit juices are beneficial for health. This study demonstrates that neither seems to be correct,” he added.

open image in gallery Orange juice was identified as the worst for blood pressure risks. But the researchers say their analysis could have mistakenly included orange-flavored drinks with added sugars ( AFP via Getty Images )

Drinking and eating better beverages can help to lower risk, the researchers say.

Replace a daily serving of a sugary beverage with whole fruit to lower the risk for high blood pressure by 22 percent, the association said. Or, replace fruit juice with whole fruit to reduce risk by 19 percent.

Milk and water also make good substitutes for sugar-sweetened beverages that can help to quench thirst. Substituting either was tied to a 13 percent lower risk.

However, the same result was not seen for replacing fruit juice with milk or water.

News.title: Messi becomes all-time leading World Cup scorer as Argentina beat Austria
News.content:
Many thought he had squandered the opportunity to break the record in the ninth minute, when Argentina were awarded a penalty after Lautaro Martínez was deemed to be fouled following a lengthy VAR check. As chants of Messi’s name rang out throughout, the captain stepped up to the spot, but saw his effort saved.

But his redemption came in the 38th minute. After helping start the move, Facundo Medina delivered a low cross from the left, and Thiago Almada cleverly dummied the ball to leave Messi with space to calmly finish into the left corner beyond Alexander Schlager.

Austria struggled to find a response, registering just one shot on target for the remainder of the match, before Messi struck again in added time to seal the victory. His persistence inside the box paid off as he found the net for his second of the night, sending the Argentina fans into mayhem.

The result sees the defending champions remain top of Group J, with tournament debutants Jordan their final group opponents, while Austria stay second and face Algeria in their last match.
